title: Families and twins: the same thing built several times
headline: Copy-paste is not this codebase's problem: 1.5% of code lines sit in 8-line clones, a scan of 3,974 files finds 41 twin pairs, and carriers, payment providers, emails, CSV, PDF and the AI tools each have one core. What matters in this area is two loading faults that every store pays at each cold start whatever it uses: both languages of the admin's words (2.8 MB built) load with 802 of 830 server entries, and three small helpers imported through the chat modules make 11 routes, the four visit beacons and the recommendations beacon among them, load 11.4 MB of server code where 1.2 to 2 MB would do. Both fixes are small and safe and come first, with a server-side import check to hold them (P0). The true duplicates are kaizenaflow.com kept twice (parity plan step 7, up to 4,400 lines, cheapest before opening), the platform's events pipeline written beside the stores', five CSV import flows and Fiken's engine copied from Tripletex's: together about 2,500 to 4,000 lines of 768,000 beyond step 7, so each is done when its area is next opened. Nothing in this plan rests on a feature being unused.

The pure lib and server split costs nothing at run time and is what lets unit tests run without a database.

findings.title: One import of sameSite through the chat module makes the four visit beacons, and five admin export routes, load the whole server core
findings.evidence: sameSite is one pure function of nine lines in src/lib/same-site.ts. chat-route.ts:38 re-exports it; its own comment says it is 'kept here for the routes that import it from here'. 57 files take it from chat-route.ts, 39 of them take nothing else, 17 already import the pure file. chat-route.ts imports ai.ts, chat-agent.ts and support.ts, and 1,307 modules follow. By static import reach (the planner's own graph): each of the four routes under /api/visit reaches 1,308 or 1,309 of 4,136 modules and 20.4 MB of source, admin-text.ts and auth.ts included; with the import pointed at the pure file they reach 146 to 150 modules and 2.7 MB, and none of the three. The bundler does not drop the re-export: the built /api/visit entry lists 117 chunks, 11.40 MB; /api/health, with 54 modules, lists 16 chunks, 1.16 MB. Requiring the beacon's chunks took 202 to 249 ms here (3 runs), health's 29 to 42 ms. New in this pass: five admin export routes are in the core for the same one line (invoices/export, reviews/export, redirects/404s/export, creators/csv, settings/close/export: about 1,308 modules today, 325 to 336 without it). For 46 of the 57 files the change is tidying: they reach the core through their real work (two of those are freed by FM-14). A scan of every re-export in src found no other that moves an entry by more than 100 modules, bar visitorKey (FM-14).
findings.cost: 11.4 MB of server JS and about 0.2 s of loading at each cold start of a beacon function, where 1.2 to 1.6 MB and 30 to 45 ms is what a route of that size takes here. Every counted page view sends a beacon, also for a page served from the cache, so these are the functions shoppers will call most.
findings.who_pays: The server at each cold start of the beacon routes, so the database write of a visit waits for it. It grows with shoppers' page views and with each deploy, not with the number of stores.
